channel.title: Kamlesh Bhagatkar: articles
channel.description: Geopolitics and current affairs from Nagpur, by politician, author and geopolitical analyst Kamlesh Bhagatkar.

item.title: RBI's Final Money Mule Rules: When Your Bank Can Put a Debit Hold, and for How Long
item.description: RBI's final rules let banks place temporary debit holds on suspected money mule accounts, with seven-day deadlines and a 31st-day release rule.

item.title: The IORA Council of Ministers Meets in Delhi: What the Delhi Communiqué Gives Bharat
item.description: IORA ministers met in New Delhi, adopted the Delhi Communiqué 2026 and endorsed two India-proposed centres of excellence. India added a $500,000 grant.

item.title: The RSS at 100: What the Sangh Is and How It Works
item.description: The RSS is a volunteer organisation founded in Nagpur in 1925. How it is organised, what a shakha does, its bans and its centenary.

item.title: The Quad: What It Is and What India Gets From It
item.description: The Quad is a grouping of India, the United States, Japan and Australia. What it does, what it is not, and what India gains.

item.title: Operation Sindoor: A Day-by-Day Timeline, 22 April to 10 May 2025
item.description: Operation Sindoor, day by day: from the Pahalgam terror attack of 22 April 2025 to the stoppage of firing on 10 May 2025.

item.title: The Indus Waters Treaty: What It Says and What "In Abeyance" Means
item.description: The Indus Waters Treaty of 1960 divides six rivers between India and Pakistan. India has held it in abeyance since 23 April 2025.

item.title: The India-EU Free Trade Agreement: What Is in It and Where It Stands
item.description: The India-EU free trade agreement was concluded on 27 January 2026 but is not yet signed or in force. What it contains and what remains.

item.title: The India-China Border Explained: The LAC, the 2020 Crisis and the 2024 Disengagement
item.description: The India-China border has no agreed line. What the LAC is, what happened at Galwan in 2020, and what the 2024 disengagement left open.

item.title: The US Proposes a 25% Tariff on India Over "Excess Capacity". Why the 17% Offer Is the Real Message
item.description: Washington proposes tariffs of up to 25% on Indian goods, or 17% with a trade deal. India rejects the excess capacity charge.

item.title: RBI's Stop Switch and Trusted Person Plan: More Control Over Your Bank Account
item.description: RBI's draft rules would let customers freeze all outgoing debits, set their own limits and name a trusted person to approve large transfers.

item.title: Modi and Merz Speak Before the India EU FTA Is Signed. What Bharat Should Watch
item.description: Germany's Chancellor called Modi three weeks before the India EU free trade agreement is due to be signed in Brussels. What is settled, and what is not.

item.title: India and Nepal Agree to Review the 1950 Treaty. What Bharat Should Bring to the Table
item.description: Modi and Balendra Shah adopted a joint vision that opens the 1950 treaty to review, with India's largest aid package for Nepal.

item.title: Balendra Shah in Delhi: What India and Nepal Can Settle, and What They Will Not
item.description: Nepal's Prime Minister Balendra Shah is in Delhi for his first bilateral visit abroad. Trains and power are on the table; the boundary is not.

item.title: DRDO's 30 kW Laser Weapon: Can India Turn a Successful Test into a Drone Shield?
item.description: DRDO's 30 kW laser, proven against drones at Kurnool, is moving towards production. Whether it reaches our units depends on industry, orders and patience.

item.title: The Siang Project and China's Medog Dam: Why India Needs Its Own Reservoir
item.description: Amit Shah promised dialogue on the 11,200 MW Siang project as local groups asked him to scrap it. China's Medog dam upstream is why India cannot drop the idea.

item.title: The Shenzhen Declaration: What Trump, Xi and Putin Agreed, and What It Means for India
item.description: The Trump, Xi and Putin meeting in Shenzhen ended in a short four-point declaration. India has taken note and is waiting for details. I think that is right.

item.title: A Pakistani Minister in Delhi, and No Change on the Indus Waters Treaty
item.description: Pakistan's climate minister came to New Delhi for the SCO forum. India's answer on the Indus Waters Treaty stayed the same: no change.

item.title: Securing the Bangladesh Border: Mobs, Smugglers and the Unfenced 864 km
item.description: A mob attack on BSF men in Tripura shows what the unfenced India Bangladesh border costs. Land, fencing and talks with Dhaka come next.

item.title: Japan Will Train at Indian Firing Ranges. What the Tokyo 2+2 Settled
item.description: India and Japan signed a Letter of Intent for Japanese forces to train at Indian firing ranges, and named economic coercion as a shared worry.

item.title: Made-in-India Shipping Containers: Can ₹10,000 Crore Loosen China's Hold?
item.description: India's ₹10,000 crore container manufacturing scheme pays makers per box and aims for 7.5 lakh TEUs a year. The test is the price gap with China.

item.title: EPFO Approves Monthly PF Payouts and Cuts the Minimum Balance to 10%
item.description: The EPFO board approved a Systematic Withdrawal Plan for retirees, a 10% minimum PF balance and a two-month wait for final withdrawal.

item.title: World Bank on India's Poverty: 27% to 2.6%, and the Work Still Ahead
item.description: The World Bank says extreme poverty in India fell from 27.1% to 2.6% between 2011 and 2023. Here is what the figures show and what they leave open.

item.title: The India Japan 2+2 in Tokyo: Test Ranges, Warships and Trust
item.description: Rajnath Singh and S Jaishankar meet their Japanese counterparts in Tokyo today. Missile test ranges, joint shipbuilding and a stealth antenna are on the table.

item.title: The Quad Summit in Manila: Patrol Planes, Sea Cables and a Forum for India
item.description: Quad leaders met in Manila after a gap of two years. They agreed on joint maritime surveillance, energy cables and a business forum India wants to host.

item.title: Why Rubio Went to Jamnagar: India's Oil Refining Power and What It Buys Us
item.description: India is the world's fourth-largest refiner. Washington pressed us over Russian oil, then sent its top diplomat to Jamnagar. Refining explains the gap.

item.title: SIM Binding for WhatsApp and Telegram: What Changes on 1 January
item.description: From 1 January 2027, messaging apps in India must stay tied to the SIM in your phone. Why the government wants it, and what it costs.

item.title: India and Egypt Agree to Explore a Trade Pact. The $12 Billion Test
item.description: India and Egypt will study a preferential or free trade agreement. Trade is recovering, but an old $12 billion target is still out of reach.

item.title: India and Somalia Hold Their First Foreign Office Talks. Why It Matters at Sea
item.description: India and Somalia have opened a formal dialogue in Mogadishu, with piracy high on the agenda. Here is what it means for our sea lanes.

item.title: China Curbs Tunnel Boring Machine Exports. India Must Make Its Own
item.description: From 18 November, China needs a licence to ship tunnel boring machines to "sensitive" countries. Here is what that means for India's tunnels and how we respond.

item.title: Qatar and Türkiye Sign a Defence Pact. What It Means for Bharat
item.description: Qatar, India's largest gas supplier, has signed a mutual defence pact with Türkiye, which is already bound to Pakistan by treaty. Here is what to watch.
